tip: Separable 'uittrekken' (take off) splits: 'ik trek mijn schoenen uit'.
An infinitive works as a noun after 'het': 'na het eten' = after eating, literally after the eating.
For time you use 'doorbrengen', to spend; keep 'uitgeven' for spending money: 'tijd doorbrengen'.
'Om ... te' plus an infinitive expresses purpose, in order to: 'om de zonsopgang te zien'.
Separable 'meenemen' splits in the present: 'neemt altijd een paraplu mee', takes an umbrella along.
The perfect of separable 'doorlezen' keeps 'ge-' inside: 'doorgelezen', read through.
Clock times take 'om': 'om zes uur' = at six o'clock.
'Doorgaans' means usually, or generally; it is a more formal version of 'meestal'.
'Inderdaad' means indeed and confirms something just said: 'inderdaad is het een mooi boek'.
'Wij danken u': 'u' is the formal you, used in polite situations.
Place 'niet' before the verbs it negates: 'hij kan morgen niet komen werken'.
'Per' names a means or rate: 'per post', by mail; 'per uur', per hour.
Motion toward a destination takes 'zijn', not 'hebben', where English uses 'have': 'zijn naar het strand gerend' (ran to the beach).
'Verdwijnen' (disappear) takes 'zijn' in the perfect: 'de zon is verdwenen'.
'Bestaan uit' means to consist of; the fixed preposition is 'uit': 'bestaat uit brood en kaas'.
'Keer' counts occurrences: 'drie keer', three times; 'twee keer', twice.
Separable 'binnensluipen' wraps 'ge-' in the perfect: 'binnengeslopen', sneaked in.
'Bovendien' means moreover, or besides, adding a further point to what came before.
Instead of a verb for 'to like doing', Dutch normally uses 'graag' plus a verb: 'verwelkomen u graag', gladly welcome.
'Hen' is the object pronoun after a verb or preposition, them: 'wij kennen hen'.
'Zich' is the reflexive pronoun; 'zich ziek melden' means to call in sick: 'zij meldt zich ziek'.
'De was' here is a noun, the laundry; it looks the same as 'was' from 'wassen' (to wash) and the past of 'zijn' (was).
'Toevoegen' is separable and takes 'aan': 'voegen extra kruiden aan de saus toe', add extra herbs to the sauce.
'Een steentje bijdragen' is a fixed phrase meaning to do your bit, to contribute your part.
'Laten zien' = to show; the two parts wrap around the object: 'laten het huis ... zien'.
'Zich verslapen' = to oversleep; it needs the reflexive 'zich': 'verslaapt zich'.
'Heen en weer' is a set phrase meaning back and forth: 'de boot vaart heen en weer'.
Separable 'ophangen' splits: 'zij hangt haar jas op', she hangs up her coat.
'Onder' means among when sharing out: 'onder de teamleden' = among the team.
Object pronoun: 'mij/me' = me – 'mij' is stressed, 'me' is unstressed.
